_what: Breaker Breaker, a shopfront on the street for CB radios, CB slang, CB history and trucking. Ryan's brief, 2026-10-24. tools/make-breaker-breaker.py writes the cab, the slang, the quotations, the rack and the credits into breaker-breaker.html from this file, and refuses what this file's rules say.
_light: Every light in the room is a marker lamp: it shows where the edge of something is and lights nothing round it. Amber at the front and sides, red at the back, which are the law's colours and not ours (Automotive lighting, below). The drawing is drawn in those two and the night, and the tool refuses any other light in it.
_left_off: Wikipedia's list of CB slang is long and some of it names people unkindly: women, sex workers, people speaking another language, people crossing the border on foot, people who ride without a helmet, and the word idiot more than once. None of it is on the page, and the tool refuses each phrase in left_off anywhere in the room. The friendly edit is to fill the board out with the rest of the list.
_records: Every record's year, label and own track lengths were read off MusicBrainz on 2026-10-24, the release named by its id, never the upload's Released on line, which gives the reissue's year (2014 for the first record). The labels are MusicBrainz's label entities written in ordinary case (KOCH is Koch, HYENA Records is Hyena Records). Every song was asked on its own watch page the same day: all of them OK, playableInEmbed true, on the artist's own channel (Dale Watson - Topic, C.W. McCall - Topic). seconds is what plays here; record is the record's.
_convoy_left_off: Convoy had a second life in 2022 as the anthem of the Freedom Convoy protests in Canada (Wikipedia's Convoy and C. W. McCall articles). The room is about the record of 1975 and the craze around it, and says nothing about 2022. Claude left it off the day the room opened, and Ryan's call the same day was to leave it off. The friendly edit is a line saying so “for completeness”; it is a change to that call, which is Ryan's.

_quote_cap: Covenstead's reason rather than the Zibaldone's: this room quotes three named passages that its own words are about, and Silberman's two sentences run to seventy-two. Eighty fits them and refuses a page. Raise it here, on purpose, with the reason written down; never to fit one passage.

quotes.words: Another community that enabled autistic people to make the most of their natural strengths in the early and mid-twentieth century was amateur radio. By routing around the face-to-face interactions they found so daunting, even people who found it nearly impossible to communicate through speech were able to reach out to kindred spirits, find potential mentors, and gain the skills and confidence they needed to become productive members of society.
quotes.work: NeuroTribes: The Legacy of Autism and the Future of Neurodiversity
quotes.checked: Read on our page Written Communication Is the Great Social Equalizer, which quotes it from the Kindle edition, pages 223 to 224, and which Ryan read on his own Kindle copy; checked against our page word for word.

quotes.words: Written communication isn’t a lesser substitute for speech. It’s a medium with its own power — one that neurodivergent people helped build, because they needed it.
quotes.work: Written Communication Is the Great Social Equalizer
quotes.checked: Our own page, checked against it word for word.

quotes.words: Similar to Internet chat rooms a quarter-century later, CB allowed people to get to know one another in a quasi-anonymous manner.

terms.means: I would like the channel. Often with its number: breaker one-nine. Then you wait for somebody to answer before you go on.
The name you go by on the air, which you choose. What’s your handle? asks somebody theirs.
Message received. Also yes, I agree: that’s a big 10-4. Four, or foe, for short.
I heard you, and I understand.
Is anybody listening? Or, with a handle in front of it, are you?
Where you are. What’s your 20? My 20 is the truck stop at the next exit.
Listening without saying anything, which is allowed.
Going quiet but still listening: 10-10 on the side.

terms.say: Wall to wall and treetop tall
terms.means: Coming in loud and clear. Five by five says it too.
All mouth and no ears: somebody who talks and never listens. A hot mic keeps the channel to themselves.
The right time, please.
A restroom break.
Best wishes, borrowed from the 73 and 88 of the amateurs’ Morse code: best regards, and hugs and kisses.
Somebody on the channel you are friendly with. The word of the 1970s.
Signing off.

terms.say: Front door, rocking chair, back door
terms.means: A group of trucks running together: the front door leads and watches ahead, the back door brings up the rear and watches behind, and the rocking chair is everybody between, who can ride easy.
Foot on the gas pedal, all the way. The hammer lane is the fast lane.
A 55 mph speed limit.
Marker lights beyond what the law asks for, on a truck dressed up with chrome to match.
Fuel. Hundred-mile coffee is very strong coffee.
A truck stop. A nap trap is a rest area.
A long strip of tyre on the road, which from a distance looks like an alligator lying in the sun.
The median, the strip down the middle of the highway.
Bad weather: fog, heavy rain or snow.
A mile marker.
A truck running without a trailer.
The trip back the other way, and going home.
Home. I’m heading back to my stack of bricks.
A state trooper, after Smokey Bear’s hat, which looks like a highway patrol’s.
Police in a plane or a helicopter.
A police officer running radar.
A weigh station, where the scales are.
A county sheriff or deputy.
Denver.
Los Angeles.
Flagstaff.
Austin.
Nashville.

_from_the_cb: Each thing the street's CB took from the citizens band is a sentence about another part of the street, so each names, in holds, words its own guide or code still says. When the radio changes, the tool stops and this list changes with it; do not delete a holds to make the tool quiet. The Community Center's service-board rule.

from_the_cb.name: A handle
from_the_cb.words: You are on the channel as a name you chose, and everybody on it knows you by it.

holds.words: On the channel as and your handle

from_the_cb.name: A channel everybody shares, and one of your own
from_the_cb.words: World is the channel the whole street shares, the way 19 is the one everybody on the interstate leaves on. Every room has a channel of its own too, this one included, the way a town on the CB used to keep a home channel, so people from there could find each other without crowding the calling channel.

holds.words: The channel the whole street shares.
The channel of the room you are standing in.

from_the_cb.name: Channel 19
from_the_cb.words: At its smallest, the radio is a drawing of a CB set on its own case with its readout on 19, and until 26 September 2026 the bar said CH 19 where Teleport is now.

holds.words: a CB set drawn on the
THE TELEPORTER, where "CH 19" used to sit.

from_the_cb.name: The squelch
from_the_cb.words: Switch on Speak new messages aloud and every message keys up with a burst of static and lets go with a tail of it, which is the sound a CB makes. At the Gentle setting you get the words without the static.

holds.words: with a burst of static before and after; at the Gentle setting, the words without the static

from_the_cb.name: Off is off
from_the_cb.words: Open and in front of you, the radio listens. Fold it away and it sends nothing, like a set switched off.

holds.words: Open is on, folded is off.

from_the_cb.name: On the air, then gone
from_the_cb.words: A CB keeps nothing: once something has been said, it has gone by. Ours keeps fifty messages, each for two weeks, and Take off takes one off the air.

holds.words: The channel keeps fifty messages, each for two weeks.
Takes the message off the air

from_the_cb.name: Reading the mail
from_the_cb.words: Listening without saying anything is fine on ours as well. Nobody is counted, and you are on Who’s online only if you press Be seen here.

holds.words: the only list of who is on is Who’s online, made from Be seen here

from_the_cb.name: BASE
from_the_cb.words: BASE beside a name is one of our moderators, after the base station, the CB set at home rather than out on the road.
